_meta.purpose: Development and demonstration dataset for the seeded market data provider.
_meta.IMPORTANT: The figures in this file are ILLUSTRATIVE AND GENERATED. Ticker symbols, company names and sector classifications are real PSX listings, but every financial figure and every price is invented for the purpose of exercising the application. They are NOT taken from any company's published accounts and must never be presented to a user as real market data. The API reports provider.is_synthetic = true so the UI can label them.
verify_real_data_at: PSX company filings and announcements (PUCARS) - https://dps.psx.com.pk/
Company annual and quarterly reports on their own investor-relations pages

profile_field_notes.latest_revenue: Revenue (PKR) for the most recent generated fiscal year.
profile_field_notes.revenue_cagr_pct: Compound annual revenue growth used to back-cast earlier years.
profile_field_notes.revenue_wobble_pct: Alternating +/- distortion applied to earlier years so growth is not unnaturally smooth; also what makes some companies read as inconsistent growers.
profile_field_notes.net_margin_pct: Net margin in the latest year.
profile_field_notes.margin_drift_pp: Change in net margin per year, in percentage points. Negative means an eroding margin.
profile_field_notes.shares_outstanding: Share count used to derive EPS from net profit.
profile_field_notes.equity_to_revenue: Shareholders' equity as a multiple of revenue.
profile_field_notes.debt_drift_pct: Annual change in gearing. Positive means debt rising faster than equity.
profile_field_notes.ocf_to_profit: Operating cash flow as a multiple of net profit. Below 1.0 means profit is not converting to cash.
profile_field_notes.capex_to_revenue: Capital expenditure as a share of revenue.
profile_field_notes.payout_ratio: Dividend as a share of EPS. 0 means no dividend.
profile_field_notes.base_price: Most recent close (PKR) the generated price series ends at.
profile_field_notes.price_trend_pct: Net price move over the generated ~15 months of sessions.
profile_field_notes.volatility_pct: Daily volatility of the generated price walk.

companies.name: Oil & Gas Development Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Pakistan's largest exploration and production company. Earns by finding, extracting and selling crude oil and natural gas, so revenue tracks both production volumes and international energy prices.

companies.name: Pakistan Petroleum Limited
companies.business_summary: Exploration and production company operating Pakistan's largest gas fields. Revenue depends on gas offtake, wellhead pricing and the pace of new discoveries.

companies.name: Pakistan State Oil Company Limited
companies.business_summary: The country's largest fuel marketing company. Buys, imports and distributes petroleum products through a retail network, so margins are thin and heavily exposed to working capital and circular debt.

companies.name: Lucky Cement Limited
companies.business_summary: Pakistan's largest cement producer, with additional interests in power, automobiles and chemicals. Earnings follow construction demand, coal costs and retail cement prices.

companies.name: D.G. Khan Cement Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Cement manufacturer with plants in Punjab and Balochistan. Highly sensitive to coal prices, interest rates on its expansion debt, and domestic construction activity.

companies.name: Maple Leaf Cement Factory Limited
companies.business_summary: Cement producer serving northern Pakistan. Recently completed a capacity expansion, so results reflect both higher volumes and the cost of financing that build-out.

companies.name: Habib Bank Limited
companies.business_summary: Pakistan's largest commercial bank. Makes money on the spread between what it pays depositors and what it earns lending or investing in government paper, plus fee income.

companies.name: MCB Bank Limited
companies.business_summary: Large commercial bank known for a high-margin deposit base and a consistent dividend record. Earnings are driven by policy rates and the mix of current versus term deposits.

companies.name: United Bank Limited
companies.business_summary: Commercial bank with a large government-securities book and a significant international remittance business.

companies.name: Meezan Bank Limited
companies.business_summary: The country's largest Islamic bank. Earns on Shariah-compliant financing and sukuk rather than conventional interest, with a fast-growing branch and deposit base.

companies.name: Fauji Fertilizer Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Urea manufacturer and marketer. Benefits from subsidised feedstock gas and inelastic farmer demand, which together produce unusually stable margins and dividends.

companies.name: Engro Fertilizers Limited
companies.business_summary: Urea and phosphate fertilizer producer. Earnings depend on gas availability, government subsidy policy and the crop cycle.

companies.name: Fatima Fertilizer Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Integrated fertilizer producer making urea, CAN and NP from its own ammonia. More exposed to international gas and input prices than peers on subsidised feedstock.

companies.name: The Hub Power Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Independent power producer with thermal and coal capacity plus investments in Thar coal mining. Cash flows are contractual but depend on being paid by the national grid.

companies.name: Kot Addu Power Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Thermal power producer whose original power purchase agreement has expired, leaving earnings dependent on how remaining capacity is contracted and on receivables recovery.

companies.name: Nestle Pakistan Limited
companies.business_summary: Packaged food and beverage manufacturer with strong brands in dairy, water and infant nutrition. Pricing power is high but volumes are sensitive to household incomes.

companies.name: Unity Foods Limited
companies.business_summary: Edible oil refiner and food commodity processor. A high-volume, very low-margin business that consumes working capital as it grows, and is exposed to palm oil prices and the rupee.

companies.name: Systems Limited
companies.business_summary: IT services and business process outsourcing exporter. Most revenue is billed in foreign currency, so results benefit from rupee depreciation but depend on client budgets abroad.

companies.name: TRG Pakistan Limited
companies.business_summary: Holding company whose value sits in stakes in overseas business process outsourcing and technology ventures rather than in its own operations, so reported results can be dominated by valuation movements.

companies.name: Indus Motor Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Assembles and sells Toyota vehicles in Pakistan. Volumes swing hard with import policy, financing rates and the rupee, since most components are imported.

companies.name: The Searle Company Limited
companies.business_summary: Pharmaceutical manufacturer selling branded generics and consumer health products. Margins are squeezed between regulated retail prices and imported active ingredients.

companies.name: Interloop Limited
companies.business_summary: Vertically integrated hosiery and apparel exporter supplying international brands. Earnings depend on export demand, cotton and energy costs, and the rupee.

companies.name: Engro Polymer & Chemicals Limited
companies.business_summary: Produces PVC and related chemicals, selling largely into construction and pipe manufacturing. A commodity business, so margins follow the global PVC-ethylene spread.

companies.name: Pak Elektron Limited
companies.business_summary: Manufactures home appliances and power distribution equipment. Consumer demand is credit-sensitive and the power division depends on utility spending, giving lumpy results.
